author: Nightowl
subject: Re: Weaponsmith: Turtle changes?
content_md:
I don't know much about professions here and it's a shame that there's no guide, but here are a few things I've noticed:
Blacksmithing:
 - 230s for a level 45 full plate (helm requires 230 smithing to use however, but the rest of 5 pieces do not). You learn this from Smithing trainers.
 - 300 for a set of full plate whose plans drop from Balnazzar. It's 6 pieces (+1 weapon plan) that are bind on pickup and require plans + 300 smithing to make. They're all level 58 and are fairy strong, though it's a dps set and not a tanking one. "Rune-etched" is the name.
 - Swordsmithing allows you to make the final piece of Rune-etched gear, the 300 swordsmith smithing runeblade. It's like 58 but is equal to revered reward from High Elf/Troll factions. Once you make you also get a lengthy epic quest that will later upgrade it to 2h sword that is slightly stronger than AV reward.
 - There are also "Deflection Shoulders" that require nothing, but it's a boss from world boss "Nerubian Overseer", they give 2% chance on hit to counterattack.

I think that is mostly it for BS, but I may be wrong, these are just the things I learned over time.

Leatherworking:
 - There are 4 pieces of leather gear designed for feral druids, "Windwalker boots" is the only one I know of, but they're all somewhere on the level of Lionheart and it's plate leggings equivalent ("Titanic leggings" I believe?) - though slightly weaker. I was however told that they're cheaper to make but I haven't confirmed that part.
 - A leveling set "Grifter" is also introduced. I believe it's 230ish like plate set. It's designed for Enhancement Shaman/Feral Druid, but others can also benefit.

Tailoring:
 - 2 leveling sets, but apparently they require 300 tailoring at least I was told that, they're all late 30s but come with spellpower, int and sometimes even hit - for dps set. Healing set is perfect for Priest because it comes with healing power, spirit and other goodies.

I think that's about it, and I'm sure that they've added more but you can't get info anywhere so you're sorta stumbling in the dark till you find out bits of info. I think it would have been better to create a compendium of all new recipes and changes in Turtle-WoW Professions.

P.S: I also think that it's bad that only Sword-wielders can get an epic sword. Would be great if they could for example add a craftable 2h mace that would benefit Shaman or Druid, or even Warrior still because he can use maces as well. One that becomes epic after a lengthy questline that is

author: Ziban
subject: Re: Plaguebloom in perma farm
content_md:
This is how herbalism works on Turtle.

There are a whole lot of potential spawn points for herbs. As a herb is picked, a new herb spawns on a random spawn point.

Therefore, herbs will tend to stay where people don't go, but will be picked quickly along popular paths.

Additionally, if you are doing a circuit "behind" another herbalist, they will pick the herbs in front of you, and the respawns will happen somewhere random ... leaving you walking thru picked-clean areas, wondering where all the Plaguebloom went.

As well, if people are "cherry picking" by - to pick a *completely random* example - leaving the Arthas' Tears and collecting the Plaguebloom, then the random spawn will be Arthas' Tears some of the time and be left as well ... and almost no Plaguebloom to be seen.

Therefore, try and go where most people dont, and try not to be following another herbalist.

Best way is to sell all raw materials on AH and buy only those things that you actually need.

Mate, you're just wrong. If you can sell an item for some gold and use your own cloth, you only need to buy the thread to craft it. You could have sold the cloth instead so missing out on the ah vendor value of your cloth is your cost of opportunity. If you buy the cloth and craft the item, you'll come out at the exact same "profit margin". It doesn't matter if you use your own cloth or buy it in the ah. There is no benefit in using your own self found cloth over ah bought.

Crafted item sells for 5G, the cloth you need is 4G. You make 1G or profit if you craft and sell the item.
a) you already had the cloth so you're turning 4G worth of cloth into a 5G item. You gained 1G by crafting the item. The 4G worth of cloth is still an expense cause you didn't sell your cloth for 4G.
b) you don't have the cloth and buy it for 4G. You're turning 4G of raw cash into a 5G item. You gained 1G by crafting the item.

There is no economical benefit using your own cloth
That's not even entry level economics, that's just common sense.

content_html:
Mate, you're just wrong. If you can sell an item for some gold and use your own cloth, you only need to buy the thread to craft it. You could have sold the cloth instead so missing out on the ah vendor value of your cloth is your cost of opportunity. If you buy the cloth and craft the item, you'll come out at the exact same "profit margin". It doesn't matter if you use your own cloth or buy it in the ah. There is no benefit in using your own self found cloth over ah bought.

Crafted item sells for 5G, the cloth you need is 4G. You make 1G or profit if you craft and sell the item.
a) you already had the cloth so you're turning 4G worth of cloth into a 5G item. You gained 1G by crafting the item. The 4G worth of cloth is still an expense cause you didn't sell your cloth for 4G.
b) you don't have the cloth and buy it for 4G. You're turning 4G of raw cash into a 5G item. You gained 1G by crafting the item.

There is no economical benefit using your own cloth
That's not even entry level economics, that's just common sense.

Cost of Mithril [https://www.wowauctions.net/auctionHous ... l-bar-3860](https://www.wowauctions.net/auctionHouse/turtle-wow/nordanaar/mergedAh/mithril-bar-3860) around 12s31c

subject: Cooking Profession - More Drinks
content_md:
![Image](https://images-ext-1.discordapp.net/external/OykEJuWZR6ZuoGapg0xTIYLVslht3OB7BcRYu3dKmoM/%3Fcb%3D20170131221206/https/static.wikia.nocookie.net/wowpedia/images/8/8e/Thistle_Tea.png/revision/latest)

Having reached 300 in cooking, I was saddened to see there was not much left available for custom Turtle Wow cooking content.

Something that was briefly touched in Classic Cooking was the inclusion of dinks I’m cooking recipes. We see these in Captain Rumsy’s Lager, Thistle Tea, Hot Apple Coder, Egg Nogg, and Goldthorn Tea. While most of these are alcoholic in nature - Thistle Tea provides an energy boost and Goldthorn Tea provides an alternative to vendor or mage water as a mana replenishing drink.

![🌙](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f319.svg) <https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Goldthorn_Tea>

I would personally like to see more drinks added to the cooking section, which would create more of a demand for herbs than just Alchemy on the auction house market. They could both provide extra mana, and potentially buffs which would be beneficial to mana users. This would encourage more to focus on the cooking skill at large.

Thank you for reading!

author: Moongirl
subject: "Predicting" Jewelcrafting
content_md:
Hi everyone! The Turtle Wow Team has announced a new profession a while back: **Jewelcrafting**! I'm quite excited for this, and I'm gathering as much gems as I could for when it releases.

Now, I still have some questions about what is actually in the list of recipes. Of course, we won't really know until it is out, but I would like to know your opinion on what is likely to appear! Here is my questions:

 **Gem Prices**: Guessing how Turtle Wow likes to make things a little difficult, I think most, if not all, recipes will need at least a gem. The team also said the "Gem Rush" (which doubles chances to find gems) will last *until* the patch. How would this affect the auction house? What about Mining Nodes? There are already 2 other professions that require mining. I feel the smart thing to do would be to add more Mining Nodes, unless the goal is for Jewelcrafters to just buy them off the auction house.

 **Dreamsteel**: Dreamsteel Bars are a type of mining bar that (I think) the Turtle Wow Team added. After looking at the database, I found out it is only used for Blacksmithing. Do you think this can be a chance to add Dreamsteel necklaces or even staves? I quite like the idea of a Dreamsteel Epic Quality Staff... (maybe because my main is a priest.)

 **Soulbound Items**: I think what some people have problems with is this: "Look, I can finally make a <item> for my alt! (Crafts <item>) Time to go to mailbox-OH NO! IT'S SOULBOUND!" (At least, that happened to me before...   turtle_tongue_head  ) I understand why the developers wouldn't want an epic item to sell on the Auction House. But Recipes? Maybe for someone like me, who barely has time for dungeons, recipes can be hard to find. I'm guessing that some recipes will be found in dungeons or even raids. Do you think they'll make the recipes soulbound as well, or just some items?

 **Jewelcrafting Companions**: I have to be honest and say, in MoP expansion, Jewelcrafting got kind of odd because you can make... gem mounts. Gem mounts that fly, nonetheless. With Turtle WoW, however, you need to have some Enchanting to make some recipes. (I'm pretty sure they said that?) Mounts are strange to me, but don't you think a little tiny gem owl following you around will be cute? What do you think are the chances for those?

Of course, this is just what I think might happen. What do you think is going to be in this new profession? I'd like to hear what you want to see or what you think is possible. Thank you for reading, and good luck on your journey!   smiling_turtle_head

author: Rudyraccoon
subject: Why even bother with getting Enchanting?
content_md:
Well, here are the things that really bother me about Enchanting.

 1. It's the biggest money sink profession.
 2. Can't sell enchantments on Auction House, have to advertise for it on trade chat
 3. People only want the best enchants, meaning no-one wants the lesser enchants.
 4. Harder to sell when more other people are selling the same thing on large servers
 5. How do you set prices?
 6. Requires raiding.

Personally this profession has always rubbed me the wrong way, like I've never gotten a character to max level and probably would struggle to do raiding, so I get the sense that this profession is probably not recommended for a casual player such as myself, and it requires a lot of salesmanship. I think I'd rather pair skinning with tailoring for any cloth class since some of the tailoring recipes require leather.

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Why even bother with getting Enchanting?
content_md:
7. To earn money with enchanting, you don't need to level it.
The only way to earn gold by enchanting is to pick it on your bank character and send him items for disenchanting. You have to install Aux and scan auction for "Shard", "Essence" and "Dust". You also should enable "disenchanting value" and "vendor price", always compare those prices and do action with highest benefit.
IIRC, Dream Dust has highest value, because it is used for high level consumables in demand. Everything else, including Illusion Dust don't profit you as much as selling green item to vendor.

In some other enchanting-related thread was a point "if enchants will be tradable on AH, then their price will go down below cost of materials".
On high level you can spend some time searching for spefic character who can enchant you best enchant.
In the same time, on low levels people don't always have lots of gold and gear is not so good to enchant it with "super best enchant". So I think that top enchants should stay as they are, but low level enchants should be made in form of items like Buckles or Armor Patches. This way, people will be able to quickly buy low level enchants from AH, without search for enchanter.

 8. I also think that all enchants should have required item level. Assuming that low levels can enchant high level enchants, then there is no demand for low level ones.
But assuming that turtle devs added Lunatic challenge and did nothing with regular enchants, I assume current status is totally fine for them.

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Is making your own gear worth it high lvl?
content_md:
Can't agree that endgame recipes are money-makers.

On the topic, I think that crafted gear is your catch-up gear if you want to equip in full blues/epics but don't want to rely on RNG of dungeons, but have ton's of gold.
Really good recipes are coming from raids, so strategy "farm recipes and make your own gear" will be harder than "farm gold and buy crafted gear". Effectively, while you spend time on farming recipes, you probably get second-grade epics and fill your items slot just fine.

author: Taralej90
subject: Re: Blacksmith shields?
content_md:
Came here to make a post about this. Goblins have a shield that's only learned via a recipe that drops from their starting zones, and it sucks.

Aaaaaaaaand that's it. No other shields at all.

As for suggestions - shields are typically made using wood (for the base), metal (for the rim and umbo) and leather (for the handle strap, optional). Shield handles are made of either wood or metal, but I suppose for QoL purposes it would be best to just ignore them and assume they're made of whatever material the shield itself is made. The wood is already available through Enchanting suppliers for wands, although if T-WoW are willing they could add separate woodworker NPCs (since Enchanting wands are only for low level).

As for stats:
"buckler" shields could lean towards agility, as they are lighter
"tower" shields could have extra block
"full metal" shields could have extra armor at the cost of agility (these should be rarer)
"kite" shields would be the standard ones

author: Buellen
subject: Re: North of theramore fishing.   Found guide from pathc 1.11 i am refrencing
content_md:
This is the article i remember reading  from around patch 1.11.  This is what i was refrencing in my post above.  Not sure i am allowed to post the link here.
all credit goes to original poster and his/her guide now posted at legacy wow site. (will post link if i am allowed)
 --------------------------------
An Introduction to Pools
Conventional “open-water” fishing is endless. There is no need to move or do anything other than cast your line and reel in your catch. Pools of fish (schools, shoals, circles, holes) are similar to other “node-based” resource gathering, such as mining ore veins. Pools appear at points in the water. Once a few (typically 3-6) fish have been caught from them, the pool disappears, and you must look for an alternative pool to fish from. Otherwise, pools remain until fished.

Pools look like swirling patches of water, clearly visible from nearby land. ((Moving the cursor over the pool will tell you what the pool contains – for example “Firefin Snapper School” mostly contain Firefin Snappers.)) To fish from a pool you must have sufficient fishing skill (with any gear or lure bonuses) to meet the base skill requirement of the area you are fishing in. Stand a short distance away from the pool, facing it, and cast. The bobber must land within the swirling water, or very close to the edge. If it doesn’t land correctly, recast until it does. There is no way to control precisely where the bobber lands, so you might need to cast several times. When the bobber splashes, reel the line in as normal to recover your fish.

 --------------------------------------------------------------

Basic Concepts
All pools are grouped into linked sets, even though they seem to be separate. Each zone has at least one set, with one set per inland or coastal area in that zone. Each set consists of a series of possible locations where a pool might appear. The number of possible locations in the set varies by area. Some sets are as low as 5 or 6 (for example, Faldir’s Cove in the Arathi Highlands), while there are 25-30 along the coasts of Feralas and the Hillsbrad Foothills. Stranglethon Vale has the greatest number of possible locations – estimated at over 50.

 ***When a pool appears it can be of any type possible in the area. For example, if an area can contain Oily Blackmouth and wreckage pools, either of these two types can appear at any of the possible pool locations.***

The probability of a specific type of pool appearing might be equal for all pool types in the same area. In the previous example, an Oily Blackmouth pool might be just as likely as a wreckage pool. This is unknown. “Cherry picking” means that you are more likely to find one pool type than another pool type.

Cherry picking involves fishing only one type of pool in an area, and leaving all the others. Once pools appear, they remain until fished completely. However, the type of pool that eventually “replaces” the one that is fished, is not decided by the type of pool that was originally fished. So in the previous example, if you were to fish only wreckage pools, and ignore the Oily Blackmouth pools, eventually there would be far more Oily Blackmouth pools to fish than wreckage pools: When a wreckage pool is fished, there is only a 50% chance of a wreckage pool appearing to “replace” it. So for every two wreckage pools you fish, only one new wreckage pool will appear. To maintain a steady supply of wreckage pools to fish, someone needs to be fishing the Oily Blackmouth pools too. For a full explanation, with evidence, see the Pool Appearance topic.

((The in-balances created by cherry picking pools are corrected once a week when the server is taken down for “maintenance”. This resets pools completely. That is why certain pools seem to be easier to find on Wednesday morning.))

The most popular theory on the appearance of pools is simple replacement: There are always the same number of pools, and when you fish one, a new one immediately appears at some other location in the set. This is true for at least some pools. For example, Sagefish in Mirkfallon Lake (Stonetalon Mountains), where there are always two pools somewhere in the lake, even after an hour of fishing Sagefish.

In most cases, the simple replacement theory is not correct. Instead, pools reappear gradually over time. How “gradually” is unknown. In the Pool Appearance topic I’ve shown that pools start reappearing about an hour after nearby pools were fished. However this might vary by location, or reflect the fact that I was the only person fishing, or some other unknown factor. There is also some evidence there that the rate of reappearance depends on how many pools currently exist in the area.

If you are routinely fishing in busy zones, where someone else was fishing before, during and after the time you fish, you will only ever see pools randomly appearing.

 -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pool Contents
Pools may contain more than just fish. All sorts of materials seem to fall from ships and cluster in pools. Any type of pool (except Elemental Water and Tastyfish) may contain Stranglekelp, trunks, or some “Rumsey” brand rum. However these are most common in wreckage pools.

The type of trunk caught depends on the zone:

Tightly Sealed Trunk – The Barrens, Darkshore, Loch Modan, Silverpine Forest, and Westfall.
Watertight Trunk – Ashenvale, Hillsbrad Foothills, Stonetalon Mountains, and Wetlands.
Iron Bound Trunk – Alterac Mountains, Arathi Highlands, Desolace, Dustwallow Marsh, and Stranglethorn Vale (north of Grom’Gol only).
Mithril Bound Trunk – Azshara, Feralas, Stranglethorn Vale (south of Grom’Gol only), and Tanaris.
The type of rum caught also depends on the zone:

Rumsey Rum Light – The Barrens, Darkshore, Loch Modan, Silverpine Forest, and Westfall.
Rumsey Rum Dark – Ashenvale, Hillsbrad Foothills, Stonetalon Mountains, and Wetlands.
Rumsey Rum Black Label – Alterac Mountains, Arathi Highlands, Azshara, Desolace, Dustwallow Marsh, Feralas, Stranglethorn Vale, and Tanaris.
Bloated fish, which often contained gems and other rare items, can no longer be caught from pools ((this was removed by patch 1.11)).

I fished 243 pools and recorded their contents ((all with patch 1.11)). These are summarised in the table below. No Deviate, Greater Sagefish, Tastyfish pools were included. Elemental Water pools are considered in the Patches of Elemental Water section. Pools were fished in many different parts of Azeroth.

author: Carlito1
subject: Fishing bug, no skill+ in schools or wreckage
content_md:
When fishing in open water such as in Stormwind or anywhere else, I achieve fishing skill up points at the rate expected for my level of fishing.

If instead I fish in pools or schools of fish, I receive no skill+ at all.

To test this I achieved 225 fishing by fishing in open water. I did the Nat Pagle quest to achieve 225/300 fishing.

I have since gone to Stranglethorn and fished over 50 Oily Blackmouth, 15 Stonescale Eel, and countless Iron Bound Trunk and Mithril Bound Trunk, from the pools around the coast.  I am still 225/300 fishing. Not a single skill-up in probably 100+ successful catches.

I asked in guild and world chat about this, and nobody seems to have encountered it. But then again, nobody really fishes.

This is 100% a bug with fishing, I'm very surprised it hasn't been raised before now.

author: Thermanshs
subject: Major Gardening design flaw, dangerously vulnerable to ninjas
content_md:
There is a major design flaw in gardening right from day I started doing it.
Any 1 lvl player can ninja the final stage of one's production by just carrying Refreshing Spring Water on him. I got it done many times by ignorant players before and had minor losses not worth mentioning. Today was maliciously camped by player already reported thru the in-game ticket system and got threatened /who "my name" and camp that place with 1 level characters and waste all production. If we are talking large scale mushroom farms that could be several hundred gold worth of loss and also several hours of play.
GM's handled the case by just messagint the player and giving a warning.
Fixing the player is not a permanent solution
Fixing the profession design is. Any 1 level character carrying 5 silver worth of vendor items can ninja several hundred gold worth of stuff
I dont think this kind of design is any benefit and very susceptible to trash player behavior like that I experienced twice today. I dont think this should be encouraged and not even allowed. Gardening loots should be looted only by the producer himself or people in his party at worst

Just my 2 cents there to make things fair and decent for everyone playing this game

The Wolfshead Helm from Tribal Leatherworking needs an improvement. Its stats are lacking.

The Wolfshead Helm should needs a stat boost: 10-13 Agi at least or straight 1% crit chance.

author: Speedz1337
subject: Gardening Guide
content_md:
This guide will show you how to garden in turtle WoW.  Survival guide is listed [here](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=114013) if you would like to know how to level survival to 75.

Gardening is picked up from [Kern Mosshoof](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?npc=51532) for horde or [Mortimer Stansfield](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?npc=51530) for alliance.  The quest to get gardening is rather straight forward and is only one quest.  You will need at least 75 skill in survival in order to pick up gardening.  Pick up You Reap What You Sow from either one of the gardening NPCs depending on your race. You can buy any of these seeds on the AH.  The magic mushroom seeds can be bought from vendors in Thunderbluff/Darnassus.  Depending on the prices on the AH buying from a vendor might be cheaper.  All the rest of the seeds have been notoriously low on the AH.

Gardening will be getting a rework soon TM.  According to this [timeline](https://turtlecraft.gg/images/roadmap_2025_2026.jpg) survival will be reworked and I believe that gardening will be reworked along with it.  Stay tuned for gardening updates in the future!

 **Gardening Tools**

To build a planter you need to use the below recipe.  You will need 75 survival to get this planter.  Buy the recipe from your respective gardener trainer in either Mulgore or Elwynn Forest.  I would recommend doing the [Mountain Berry Bush Seeds](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51707) or the [Magic Mushroom Spores](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51716) due to the rewards listed at the bottom of the guide.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/CMTSbHU.png)

 **Seeds**

[![Image](https://i.imgur.com/FhLxB6z.png)](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51707)
- Mountain Berry Bush Seeds: These are collected from [bushes](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?object=1000371) around The Hinterlands. They can also be bought on the AH.
[![Image](https://i.imgur.com/oaB0nti.png)](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51706)
- Country Pumpkin Seeds: These are collected from [garden pumpkins](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?object=1000370) in three zones.   Elwynn Forest, Tirisfal Glades, and Hilsbrad Foothills are the three zones that these seeds can be found in.  They can also be bought on the AH.
[![Image](https://i.imgur.com/o3ZTUc2.png)](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51708)
- Striped Melon Seeds: These are collected from [ripe garden watermelons](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?object=1000372) in five zones. The Barrens, Durotar, Elwynn Forest, Redridge Mountains, and Mulgore are the five zones that these seeds can be found in.  They can also be bought on the AH.
[![Image](https://i.imgur.com/sz9CmIH.png)](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51716)
- Magic Mushroom Spores: These are bought from three vendors.  Mulgore, Teldrassil and Eastern Plaguelands are the three zones that the vendors are located at.  The AH might have lower values than the vendor prices.  Vendor price sits at 2 gold 50 silver.  When you account for the 20% discount it will be 2 gold instead.
 **Gardening Stages**

Each stage takes 9 minutes to progress to the next stage.  The planter can be placed in only specific locations which I will outline at the bottom of this guide.  But for now you can place Simple Wooden Planters that you make from survival profession at the gardening start NPCs.  The initial planter looks like the image below.  This means that each seed will take 36 minutes to mature (with no downtime between stages).  The in between stages cannot be spoiled by time.  The planters seem to disappear when you logout or leave the zone no matter what stage you are in.

The planters take 1 seed each.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/wYwjPKq.png)

 **Small shrub of berries. Looks promising.**

This stage takes 9 minutes to mature into the next stage.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/YIOCqV4.png)

 **Small shrub of berries. Soil needed.**

After you put Un'goro Soil to fertilize your plant there will be a 9 minute window till the next stage.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/yYytVAZ.png)

 **Growing bush of berries. Water it!**

You will need Refreshing Spring Water to water this stage of the cycle. Another 9 minutes later.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/NjgXlXZ.png)

 **Berry bush is growing!**

Once this cycle is complete you will need to water this one more time.  After that the bush will be ready for harvest.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/IHOyimr.png)

 **Bush full of berries. Harvest it!**

You will gain 2 different types of Mountain Berries.  Each with their own seperate food buff and quantities in each bush.  You will get between 3-6 berries of each type.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/2yG9XRx.png)

 **Rewards from Gardening**

The above gardening stages apply to all 4 seed variations.  The planters look different for each stage but the required materials and durations are the same. Below are the rewards for each of the 4 variations of seeds.

 **Mountain Berry Bush Seeds**

Sour Mountain Berry (3-6 Berries)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/jNGTeO3.png)

Sweet Mountain Berry (3-6 Berries)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/STj1ktJ.png)

 **Country Pumpkin Seeds**

Plump Country Pumpkin (3-6 Pumpkins) This version only gives 6 stam and spirit flat.
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/L3rUqZr.png)

Plump Country Pumpkin (3-6 Pumpkins) This version gives 25% stam and spirit of your level.
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/obtadbC.png)

 **Striped Melon Seeds**

Juicy Striped Melon (3-6 Melons)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/R1VrxVH.png)

Juicy Striped Melon (3-6 Melons)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/xLPbSPx.png)

 **Magic Mushroom Spores**

Hardened Mushroom (2-5 Mushrooms)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/AUidphK.png)

Power Mushroom (2-5 Mushrooms)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/oJAnpj9.png)

 **Locations for Gardening**

You can put down gardening planters anywhere in the world besides main cities.  Below is an outdated map of all the zones that used to be restricted for gardening.
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/0HRXrg3.png) ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/LTkUBPL.png)

[![Image](https://i.imgur.com/haOMSXL.png)](https://buymeacoffee.com/speedz)

This stage takes 9 minutes to mature into the next stage.



Small shrub of berries. Soil needed.

Growing bush of berries. Water it!

You will need Refreshing Spring Water to water this stage of the cycle. Another 9 minutes later.



Berry bush is growing!

Once this cycle is complete you will need to water this one more time. After that the bush will be ready for harvest.



Bush full of berries. Harvest it!

You will gain 2 different types of Mountain Berries. Each with their own seperate food buff and quantities in each bush. You will get between 3-6 berries of each type.

Magic Mushroom Spores

author: Cosmico
subject: Low lvl enchants rude prices
content_md:
Hereby I summon the law of the 50-50: I agreed to play, I have a voice.

Look... it is nuts that you have to pay 4G for 1/? pieces of an enchantment for new player gear leveling.

The fact is that I feel the urge to acquire the minimum enchantments for Gilneas at minimum level. And the surprise was that's impossible. Maybe and just maybe, by getting pieces to disenchant materials to enchant 8 pieces of gear it might cost 15g not less.

And don't get a misunderstanding here, this is not a rant to get compassion or get discounts for a special treatment.

For all the community content I've seen so far in the different medias I was told turtle was the "ninth marvel" of the genre. However, that's not accurate. A big majority of the community at least in south seas is already or about 60 lvl, and all the economy is driven to this, and alts. Out of guild "generosity" it's impossible for you to reach the market to start the journey.

 15G just for enchantments on pieces that surely will be replaces in 5 lvls or 10, is an exaggerated number if we consider that gilneas missions with all the investment and time they require, will deliver no more than 1G.

People will say it's unfair but that's how it is. Others (because I've already gone through that) will say just don't enchant for now.

My conclusion is very simple for this approach in reaction to alts and 60 lvl economy, maybe you got out from retail, but you didn't take retail out of you.

author: Azcron
subject: Re: Low lvl enchants rude prices
content_md:
You’re absolutely right to feel the weight of the early-game economy. 15g for basic enchantments when you're trying to enjoy Gilneas in the 40s is steep, especially when quest rewards barely cover a few silver. It’s discouraging when you want to immerse yourself, to feel like your character matters in this world — but you’re met with a wall of inflation, high-level-driven pricing, and a player economy that doesn’t seem to make room for newcomers.

That said, here’s another way to look at it:

Turtle WoW isn’t just “retail in disguise” — it’s a community sandbox, and economies in sandboxes take time to find balance. Yes, many players are 60. Yes, the market is flooded with high-level gear, gold, and expectations. But that’s not necessarily a flaw of the system — it’s just a phase of its life. You’re stepping into a world that’s already living and breathing. That can feel alienating, but also — it’s an opportunity.

The economy wasn’t built for levelers anymore, but guilds, communities, and even crafting groups exist precisely to patch that gap. Turtle, unlike retail, gives you time. Time to find people who value helping lowbies, time to meet crafters who’ll enchant for free or cheap just to support someone enjoying the journey. Not every slot needs enchanting right away — and maybe that’s part of the charm. You’ll get there piece by piece, not instantly — and when you do, it’ll mean something.

Also, the cost of enchantments doesn’t have to be an expectation — it’s a choice. Leveling can still be engaging and powerful without every piece of gear glimmering with stats. In a way, that’s the anti-retail heart of Turtle: the stats don’t make the story, you do.

So yeah — it’s frustrating, but also, you’re not alone in that. Many had to wrestle with the same economy, and many have found ways to thrive by leaning into Turtle’s slower, communal pace.

Don’t give up on the world just because the auction house is cold. Gilneas is waiting. And so is the journey that doesn't need +4 spellpower to start meaning something.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Level 300 fishing still failing to catch fish in most areas
content_md:
The highest bracket of fishing areas (Bay of Storms, Winterspring, Zul'Gurub, etc) requires 330 skill to cast, and 425 skill to guarantee success.

If you have BiS fishing gear (+35 from rod, +5 from line, +5 from hat, +5 from boots) you can get away with +75 lures, otherwise you have to use the +100 lures to guarantee success. There should be +50 from deploying a fishing boat, but I've seen many reports that it's bugged right now.

If by "failed casts" you mean an empty loot window (or rather just the sound of a loot window opening) that's a different issue. You passed the skill check, but some fishing loot tables don't add up to 100%, so you can roll empty loot (happens on Tel'Abim as well for instance). It's technically a successful fishing attempt, it just didn't award you with an item, hence why you don't get an error message.

author: Singran
subject: Idea to Make Leatherworking More Useful in Raids
content_md:
Hello everyone, and hello dear game designers,

I would like to discuss the imbalance between Leatherworking and other professions. In the next patch, both Blacksmithing and Leatherworking will receive some new recipes, but Leatherworking still feels less effective in end-game content compared to other professions.

Currently, Leatherworking has some recipes for Kara40 and a kit for spell damage.

Could you please take a look at this small issue and perhaps consider adding a few new features — for example, Drums that could give a 5% casting speed boost to the party for a few seconds, or other small bonuses that wouldn’t be game-changing for high-end content but would make Leatherworkers more useful in raids.

I believe this would add some fresh flavor to gameplay and make high-end content more varied.

P.S. Thank you for all the changes you’ve made for us — it’s a great job, and you’re still giving us so much more to experience in a game that’s over 20 years old.

author: Metaalverf
subject: Re: Craftmaster challenge as Hunter. Tips?
content_md:
Is ammo restricted by the challenge?

Leatherworking has  its own mail armor pieces beyond skill
 200 I think. Most of those recipes drop in tanaris. So it could be worth sticking to LW slightly longer.

Bags are not a part of the challenge, but if you feel like they should, you must get tailor early on.

Blacksmithing can get you decent melee weapons, even for hunters.

author: Blysk990223
subject: Re: Making us some gold
content_md: If you're asking about professions in the game, it's not the best, but if I were focusing solely on making money from them, I'd choose mining/herbalism + skinning and sell everything I acquire. You can always focus on killing specific enemies, such as Elemental Earth (Badlands, Arathi Highlands) or Essence of Fire (Un'Goro). Not every character class allows for this type of income, but you can focus on farming solo AOE instances like Mara Princess Run or ZF. If you're a mage/paladin, you can boost people for gold. I've been playing for 20 years and have a lot of experience, so my favorite way to make money is the Auction House (AH) and trading. Buying low and selling high (flipping), observing trends (e.g., potions rising in price before raid night), and monitoring the market for rare materials (e.g., Mooncloth, Black Lotus). Playing on the AH isn't for everyone, as you need a budget to get started. There's also the risk of spending a lot of gold on materials that will ultimately cost you money. However, I believe that if someone has a good understanding of the game, understands how certain systems work, understands the decreasing or increasing demand for a specific item, and can generate an item deficit on the AH, they'll be able to snowball their gold very quickly. I currently have 918g at level 56.

author: Surtugal
subject: Re: Don't do mining and blacksmithing
content_md:
All professions that produce gear suffer from the same problem. They are flawed at the most fundamental design level.

>>There is no irreversible wear on equipment in WoW.

As a result, there is no naturally (supply and demand) regulated economy for equipment. Demand for equipment is artificially stimulated by new characters. No new characters, no new gear.

The situation is different for consumables. As the name suggests, these are consumed.

This means that on a permanent server like Twow, all prices for gear will eventually settle at a low level, while all the cash that is free floating in that economy can flow into the other professions or other gold sinks. Turtle wow tackled some of the issues with more „enchant“ type consumables but the imbalance remains.
Dunno if my theory holds , because enchanting is still kinda expensive (but less than I remember tbh)

author: Farehorn
subject: Fishing needs improvements
content_md:
Hey

I am a huge fan of fishing in blizz wow and have been fishing also here in Turtle. But the biggest thing that bugs me with this is that it is not rewarding and it is really monotonious. There are actually no rewards but the actual fish after you reach 300 and win STV contest. Sure some of the fish sell well, but its still just... casting.

I really think fishing needs some love as a trade skill. Here are couple of ideas:
 - Quests that require fishing
 - New fish, maybe even uncommon, rare and epic fish
 - New lure types (eg. lure out day fishes during night and vice versa, etc.)
 - Chum, that you can make with survival to throw in water to summon a pool of fish suited to area. Different animal meats would produce different type of chum. Would work nice with survival skill as a support for fishing.
 - New contests
 - Guttable fish which produce items for recipes and contains sometimes items that the fish has eaten, like jewellry or gems.
 - Improved loot from lock boxes (it really sucks currently!)
 - New fish like Deviate fish that can be used to do cosmetic stuff
 - Include fish in more alchemy and other recipes
 - etc.

It really should be revamped. It is now too plain profession with nothing but casting to do.

Oh, and the leveling bug should be fixed.

author: Retaz
subject: Vanilla Mining Guide 1–300 : Alliance & Horde Routes
content_md:
**Alliance Mining Routes:**

 **1–65 (Copper):[/size]**
- Elwynn Forest: Stick to the outer ring for dense Copper veins.

Dun Morogh: Southern hills and small caves offer good Copper spawns.
 **65–125 (Tin & Copper):**
- Redridge Mountains: Follow the mountain ridges for Tin, Copper along rivers.

Loch Modan: Hills and cliffsides have a mix of Tin and Copper veins.
 **125–175 (Iron & Gold):**
- Arathi Highlands: Hillsides and cliffs, some Gold near rivers.

Thousand Needles: Canyon walls and mesas are great for Iron and occasional Gold.
 **175–245 (Mithril & Truesilver):**
- The Hinterlands: Loop around mountain areas for Mithril.

Tanaris: Desert cliffs and rock formations are rich in Mithril.
 **245–300 (Thorium):**
- Un’Goro Crater: Outer edges, cliffs, and caves for Thorium.

Eastern Plaguelands: Light’s Hope Chapel to Plaguewood circuit.

Winterspring: Mountain ridges near Everlook for final Thorium veins.
 **Horde Mining Routes:**

 **1–65 (Copper):**
- Durotar: Valley areas between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar.

Mulgore: Circular routes around Thunder Bluff for dense Copper.

Tirisfal Glades: Hills and rivers near Brill, low competition.
 **65–125 (Tin & Silver):**
- The Barrens: Follow paths between the crossroad and Fort Triumph.

Hillsbrad Foothills: Hillsides and riverbanks for Silver and Tin.
 **125–175 (Iron & Gold):**
Arathi Highlands: Hills and cliffs for Iron; Gold near rivers.

Thousand Needles: Canyon walls provide good Iron spawns.

 **175–245 (Mithril & Truesilver):**
- Desolace: Cliffs and mountains for Mithril.

Tanaris: Desert rocks and cliffs rich in Mithril
.

 **245–300 (Thorium):**
- Un’Goro Crater: Outer cliffs and caves for Thorium.

Eastern Plaguelands: Circuit from Light’s Hope Chapel to Plaguewood.
Felwood: High-level Thorium nodes in corrupted forests.

If you found this guide helpful, feel free to leave a comment or share your own farming routes! Every tip helps the community, and I’d love to see all your hard work showcased.  turtle_in_love

author: Retaz
subject: 🐢 Complete Turtle WoW Engineering Guide 1-300
content_md:
Engineering is not just a profession; it’s a way of life in WoW Classic. From raid-winning explosives to game-changing PvP trinkets, no other craft offers the sheer power and utility of Engineering. This blueprint will guide you through the quickest and most cost-effective path to max skill.

![🎯](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f3af.svg) **Why Engineering? (The Endgame Goal)**
Before you start, understand what max skill unlocks:

PvE DPS: The Goblin Sapper Charge (Goblin Specialization) is mandatory for optimal AoE damage in dungeons and speed running. The Gnomish Battle Chicken (Gnomish Specialization) provides a valuable Melee Haste buff.

PvP Mastery: Items like Iron Grenade (AoE Stun), Gnomish Net-o-Matic Projector (Root), and Reflectors (e.g., Gyrofreeze Ice Reflector) give you a significant, game-breaking advantage in duels and World PvP.

Utility: Field Repair Bot 74A (mobile repairs), Seaforium Charges (opening locked chests/doors), and Jumper Cables (combat resurrection attempt).

![🛒](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f6d2.svg) The Comprehensive Shopping List
Always remember to save components. The entire leveling path is designed to use low-level creations to fuel high-level ones.

<https://ibb.co/Ld6hVsHJ>

![🚀](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f680.svg) **Leveling Path: Step-by-Step Instructions**
 1. Apprentice (1 – 75): Copper & Components
 1 – 50: Your first 50 points come from crafting base components that must be saved:

Craft Rough Blasting Powder (60x)

Craft Handful of Copper Bolts (30x)

 50 – 51: Craft Arclight Spanner (1x). KEEP THIS TOOL! You need it to craft many items.

 51 – 75: Craft Rough Copper Bomb (~30x). This uses your saved powder and bolts.

 2. Journeyman (75 – 150): Bronze & Frameworks
T:LearnJourneymanEngineeringatskill50,requiresLevel10+
 75 – 100: Craft Coarse Blasting Powder (60x) and use them to make Coarse Dynamite (~20x).

 100 – 125: Craft Silver Contact (5x) and Bronze Tube (25x). SAVE THE TUBES!

 125 – 135: Craft Standard Scope (10x).

 135 – 175: This is a component-heavy step:

Craft Heavy Blasting Powder (30x), Whirring Bronze Gizmo (15x), and Bronze Framework (15x). SAVE THEM ALL.

Use all the saved components to craft Explosive Sheep (15x).

 3. Expert Engineer (150 – 225): Tools & Mithril
T:LearnExpertEngineeringatskill125,requiresLevel20+
 175 – 176: Craft Gyromatic Micro-Adjustor (1x). KEEP THIS SECOND TOOL!

 176 – 200: Craft Solid Blasting Powder (60x). SAVE! Finish with a few Mithril Tube (~7x).

 200 – 250: The Mithril section. Again, craft components first:

Craft Unstable Trigger (20x) and Mithril Casing (40x). SAVE BOTH.

Use these saved components, plus Solid Blasting Powder, to craft Hi-Explosive Bomb (20x).

 4. Artisan Engineer (225 – 300): The Final Push
T:Travelto∗∗BuzzekBracketswing∗∗in∗∗Gadgetzan,Tanaris∗∗(Horde/Alliance)tolearnArtisanEngineering.RequiresLevel35+
 250 – 260: Craft Dense Blasting Powder (30x). SAVE!

 260 – 285: Thorium Widget (~35x) is your best skill-up. The Schematic is sold by vendors in Orgrimmar/Ironforge.

 285 – 300: Finish with Thorium Shells (15x) or Thorium Tube. The Thorium Shells schematic is a BoE World Drop and can be expensive. Check the AH or opt for the easier Thorium Tube.

![⚙️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2699.svg) The Critical Choice: Specialization at 200 (Level 30)
Once you hit Skill 200 and Level 30, you face the most important decision: Goblin or Gnomish Engineering. This choice is permanent without the expensive and time-consuming process of unlearning and re-leveling.

Gnomish Engineering (Utility and Control)
- Focus: Clever gadgets, utility, control tools, and unpredictable, fun effects.

Key BoP Item: The Gnomish Battle Chicken. This is critical as it provides a party-wide Melee Haste buff, making Gnomish desirable for many Melee DPS in competitive PvE.

Teleporter: Ultrasafe Transporter: Gadgetzan (Tanaris). Useful for quick access to the neutral city hub.

Ideal For: Melee DPS (due to the Chicken), players who prioritize utility over pure damage, and General PvP.
Goblin Engineering (Destruction and Explosives)
- Focus: Pure destructive power, high damage, and high-risk maneuvers.

Key Consumable: Goblin Sapper Charge. This is the most crucial item, providing massive AoE damage essential for tank threat and dungeon/raid speed runs.

Key BoP Item: Goblin Jumper Cables XL (offers a higher chance of combat resurrection success compared to the regular version).

Teleporter: Dimensional Ripper - Everlook (Winterspring). Closer to the Songflower buff area, which can be useful.
if you want more detail check [goblin vs gnomish engineering guide](https://noobtoboss.com/wow-classic-engineering-guide-gnomish-goblin/)

Understood. Here are the two new sections (Gold Making and Pairing) translated and formatted for your English forum post, ready to be inserted before the final conclusion.

![💰](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f4b0.svg) **Gold Making: Is Engineering Profitable?**
Engineering is traditionally a profession for personal use and optimization, not for direct income generation. Unlike Tailoring (Bags) or Alchemy (Potions), most Engineering items are crafted for the Engineer's own benefit.

However, there are key opportunities for making gold:

Explosives Bulk Sales:

If you are a Goblin Engineer, crafting Goblin Sapper Charges and Dense Dynamite in bulk and selling them to raiding guilds can generate decent profit. This is especially true during phases that demand high AoE damage.

Ammunition & Scopes (Hunter Market):

Crafting Thorium Shells/Arrows and high-end scopes like the Biznicks 247x128 Accurascope provides a steady, reliable income stream. These are consumables that Hunters constantly need.

Utility Gadgets:

Bound on Equip (BoE) items like the Gnomish Alarm-o-Bot (to detect rogues/druids) or early-game helms can be sold on the Auction House, though the profit margin is often small.

Gold Making Summary: The true financial benefit of Engineering is in the cost savings. By crafting all your own essential tools (bombs, transporters, scopes), you will save thousands of gold that you would otherwise spend on the Auction House.

![⛏️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/26cf.svg) **Best Profession Pairing: What Should I Take With Engineering?**
The choice for the best secondary profession to pair with Engineering is overwhelmingly clear:

Mining: The Essential Pairing
The Reason: Engineering is entirely dependent on Ore and Stone for every skill point from 1 to 300.

You need Mining to gather the raw materials for Copper, Bronze, Mithril, and Thorium Bars.

All the necessary Blasting Powders (Rough, Coarse, Heavy, Solid, Dense), which make up the vast majority of your skill-ups, are crafted directly from the Stone you gather while Mining.

Cost Efficiency: Without Mining, you will be forced to buy every single piece of ore and stone from the Auction House, which will quadruple the cost of leveling Engineering.

Can I pair it with anything else?

Yes, if your goal is purely financial, you could pair Engineering with another gathering profession like Herbalism or Skinning and sell those raw materials to fund your Engineering level. However, this is significantly less time-efficient than just gathering your own Engineering materials via Mining.

Why Engineering? (The Endgame Goal)
Before you start, understand what max skill unlocks:

PvE DPS: The Goblin Sapper Charge (Goblin Specialization) is mandatory for optimal AoE damage in dungeons and speed running. The Gnomish Battle Chicken (Gnomish Specialization) provides a valuable Melee Haste buff.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Re: Is this Right on Blacksmith?
content_md:
If you take a step back and look at the Runic Plate set as a whole, the pattern isn't just clear — it’s honestly a bit baffling.

Every single piece follows the same punishing logic: they’re all Bind on Pickup, they all require 300 Blacksmithing, and they only drop from high-level elites or rares tucked away in some of the most inconvenient corners of the map.

 **The "Out of the Way" Problem**

Think about where you actually have to go to get these.

 **Alcaz Island:** You’re trekking out to Dustwallow Marsh to farm Strashaz mobs for the helm and shoulders. Unless you're deep into the Scarab Lord grind, there is zero reason to be there. It’s a ghost town for a reason.

 **Hearthglen:** For the leggings, you’re diving into a level 59 rare elite inside a fortified Scarlet Crusade stronghold.

 **The World:** The boots are another elite drop in a hostile zone.

This isn't gear you "stumble upon" while leveling. This is gear you have to go out of your way to target-farm, which usually means dragging a group along to help you kill elites just so you can get a BoP recipe.

 **The Math Doesn't Add Up**

Then you look at the crafting cost. We’re talking two Arcanite Bars per piece. In any version of the game where these materials matter, that is a massive investment. And for what? A green item.

The comparison to Blackrock Depths (BRD) is where the argument for Runic Plate completely falls apart:

 **Accessibility:** Most players are running BRD anyway for pre-raid BiS or attunements. You get gear there just by playing the game.

 **Specialization:** The Runic set tries to split its budget between Fire and Nature resistance. That’s just bad design. You almost never need both at the same time. If you need Fire res, you go Dark Iron. If you need Nature, you go Ironvine. Both of those sets blow Runic Plate out of the water.

 **The Verdict**

It’s a classic case of "High Effort, Low Reward." It unlocks too late to be useful for progression, costs too much to be a "budget" option, and the stats are too diluted to be optimal for raiding.

At the end of the day, it’s not just that the set is hard to get — it’s that it has no home. It’s a relic of early design that doesn't have a clear purpose in the modern game flow.
content_html:
If you take a step back and look at the Runic Plate set as a whole, the pattern isn't just clear — it’s honestly a bit baffling.

Every single piece follows the same punishing logic: they’re all Bind on Pickup, they all require 300 Blacksmithing, and they only drop from high-level elites or rares tucked away in some of the most inconvenient corners of the map.

The "Out of the Way" Problem

Think about where you actually have to go to get these.

Alcaz Island: You’re trekking out to Dustwallow Marsh to farm Strashaz mobs for the helm and shoulders. Unless you're deep into the Scarab Lord grind, there is zero reason to be there. It’s a ghost town for a reason.

Hearthglen: For the leggings, you’re diving into a level 59 rare elite inside a fortified Scarlet Crusade stronghold.

The World: The boots are another elite drop in a hostile zone.

This isn't gear you "stumble upon" while leveling. This is gear you have to go out of your way to target-farm, which usually means dragging a group along to help you kill elites just so you can get a BoP recipe.

The Math Doesn't Add Up

Then you look at the crafting cost. We’re talking two Arcanite Bars per piece. In any version of the game where these materials matter, that is a massive investment. And for what? A green item.

The comparison to Blackrock Depths (BRD) is where the argument for Runic Plate completely falls apart:

Accessibility: Most players are running BRD anyway for pre-raid BiS or attunements. You get gear there just by playing the game.

The Verdict

It’s a classic case of "High Effort, Low Reward." It unlocks too late to be useful for progression, costs too much to be a "budget" option, and the stats are too diluted to be optimal for raiding.

At the end of the day, it’s not just that the set is hard to get — it’s that it has no home. It’s a relic of early design that doesn't have a clear purpose in the modern game flow.

author: Elesion
subject: Survival is awesome!
content_md:
With all the negativity going around, I'd like to talk about something that I really enjoyed about the most recent patch - Survival!

- Available to everyone - no FOMO, no having to delete established professions.
- Has fun toys, but also useful products.
- Ties into other professions well, even into secondary professions.
- Secret pets.
- Adds a fun gathering activity without having to expend a profession slot.
- New trees fit super well into the established world.
- And all of that actually integrates into the player economy!
Professions have been hurt time after time across the years, most egregiously by the weekly lootboxes introduced with the 1.18 patch. Instead of tackling the complex problem of fixing the player-driven economy suddenly we had materials and finished products spawn out of thin air without even having to level any professions, which utterly ruined some professions and made farming unattractive.
I'm very happy to see Survival go the other route again. Wood was removed from vendors and added to a gathering activity. How lovely! One of my favorite aspects about WoW is riding around, stocking up on resources and feeling you're meaningfully contributing to the community by providing a service to those who can't or don't want to gather themselves - while at the same time also lining your pockets and furthering your own character development.
And not only that, Survival can even boost your herb gathering and mining through special trinkets! This is the correct way to tackle something like Black Lotus scarcity - make gathering more rewarding instead of just conjuring mats from unrelated activities.

Survival has easily been the best part of the patch for me and it is very much a step in the right direction for the server. Thank you for that!

Please don't forget us, because this is really infuriating.

content_md:
Honestly yeah perhaps my database isn't big enough, but I feel like it definitely should be buffed.
On classic I had an avg of 1-2 arcane crystals /hour ( Which is about 150g/h )
Here, after farming 2 professions to max and farming for more than an hour, i made on avg 30g.
Let's say that i made 2 arcane crystals, that's only 50g.
I'm not saying we should make 150g/hour, classic auction house was busted and fucked up.

But if you simply look at the time spend and return, this is just really worthless.
When you know that JC can simply prospect dense stone ( Which you can buy on AH ) and get arcane crystals by litterally doing nothing...
Don't forget that on top of that, we have no layering so there's even less ores available.

Mining just feels like a waste of time, lasher farming looks like the only "available" option.
( That is if you buy a seller for money ofc )

author: Scootiesana
subject: Plans: Dragonscale Belt Buckle - is this even worth the trouble?
content_md:
Hey everyone,

After the dev team allowed us to access the database again I went out to search for the location of the new belt buckles, see if I can farm them.

To my surprise, there was a new one I didn't know about, Plans: Dragonscale Belt Buckle, problem is, the current drop rate is like 1 in 4000 kills.

I went out and killed like 200-300 dragons for it, thinking the drop rate was an exageration and with the passing of days the drop % will change in the database but it hasn't.

At this rate I have to ask, what's the point of such extremly low world drop rate?

There are lots and lots of blacksmith and enchant plans I know about that have around 1 or 2% chance from specific world npc's but I have to admit it's the first time I see a drop rate this low.

Why?
